messages:
mira: Heads-up — I'm sketching a proposal for per-org 'budgeted QoS' + spillover into a shared pool when an org's reserved tokens are exhausted. Goal: keep latencies predictable for paid tiers while allowing utilization gains during slack periods.

ashwin: high-level — are we doing token-bucket or leaky-bucket? which signals control refill rates?

mira: thinking hybrid. steady leaky-bucket (smooths sustained load) + burst token-bucket for short spikes. refill tied to regional GPU headroom metric (gpu_free_slots or pct_idle).

devon: question — spillover to shared pool sounds fine, but how do we avoid noisy orgs starving others? we need weighted fairness and preemption rules.

mira: agree. plan: per-org weights, and shared-pool uses weighted fair share; plus cost-priority tiers: spillover can be routed to lower-cost model variants (quantized) when under heavy load.

ashwin: can you post a sample config? want to validate SRE/Autoscaling interactions.

mira: example config snippet:
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "steady_rate_rps": 10,
  "burst_tokens": 500,
  "burst_refill_per_min": 100,
  "spill_to_shared": true,
  "spill_priority": ["low_cost_models", "regional_peers"],
  "max_queue_ms": 500,
  "hedging_delay_ms": 120
}
```

devon: max_queue_ms 500 seems high for interactive flows. we should make that per-route (chat vs embeddings). embeddings can tolerate seconds, chat needs <150ms ideally.

mira: yes per-route overrides planned. also hedging: if queued > hedging_delay_ms and local capacity < 20%, re-route to regional peer or low-cost variant and tag with cost_source.

ashwin: multi-region spill concerns: network egress and P95 jump. proposal: prefer cross-region only when cost delta allowed and only for non-PII workloads. telemetry must tag region and cost.

mira: exactly. policy: local -> regional same-cloud -> cross-cloud (last resort). fallback tags added so billing/sla show the deviation.

devon: admission control math — we need to map GPU slots to token refill. propose a controller that publishes a per-region "refill_rate_rps" derived from free_k80_equivalents and recent token consumption.

tal: from SRE: we need clear saturation signals to avoid oscillation. use smoothed 30s window for free slots, and enforce a min_recovery_delay after refill jumps. alerts: queue_depth > 1000 or refill_rate drops 50% in 1m.

mira: noted. also adding emergency shedding: when region enters critical <5% free we deny non-SLA traffic and drain spillover to other regions if allowed.

ashwin: how does this interact with rate-limits tied to API keys/orgs? do we still enforce hard per-key caps?

mira: yes — hard caps remain for abuse control. budgeted QoS sits above those caps as an operational throttle that can be relaxed via spillover. if org uses spillover credits, we annotate usage for billing and flag for quota review.

devon: we should simulate with a few traffic shapes: steady high, bursty, and cascading failures. also run game days where one region loses 30% capacity.

mira: plan: prototype controller + simulator. initial canary: 5 orgs across two regions, enable spillover with cost tags. owner: mira.

infra-bot: deploy-check — canary flag "budgeted_qos_spillover" exists in feature-flags service. runbooks: ops/runbooks/budgeted-qos.md (draft).

ops-bot: rollout plan: canary 5% orgs for 48h, monitor queue_depth, p95_latency, spillover_rate. automated rollback if p95 increases >20% or error_rate >1%.

ashwin: :thumbsup: Sounds good. one ask — include model-variant mapping in the config so spill->lower-cost is deterministic.

mira: will add. thanks all — will push a design doc and simulation results by Monday. owner still me.

devon: :thinking_face: also add cost-estimate model for cross-region egress.

tal: will prep alerts and dashboards for the canary.

mira: cool — we'll sync Monday in infra sync, and I'll attach the simulator and sample datasets.

infra-bot: note: thread archived to infra/architecture after final doc posted.
